body:
## Is this Newcastle office ready for a fitout?

A tenancy can look presentable and still need substantial investigation or work before it suits your business. Fitout readiness means understanding the gap between the existing premises and your intended workplace, with evidence, responsibilities and budget assumptions recorded before you commit.

Your Office Space provides client-side project management. We help organise the agreed brief, information, appointments, decisions and programme on the business's behalf. YOS does not carry out fitout construction as principal contractor, determine planning approval or certify that a building is safe to occupy. The appointed contractors and appropriately qualified advisers retain their respective roles.

[BUTTON: Plan my Newcastle fitout brief]

**Free working pack:** [Download the two-page checklist (PDF)](/guides/office-fitout-readiness-newcastle-checklist.pdf) or [use the editable text version](/guides/office-fitout-readiness-newcastle-checklist.txt). No email is required. The pack records questions, evidence and decisions for discussion with your appointed team; it is not an approval or safety certificate.

## Define what ready means for your business

Start with the work your people need to do, the busiest normal day, visitors, rooms, equipment, storage and target operating date. Record the furniture and equipment you intend to keep. Then test those needs against a measured plan and the existing building information.

A property advertised as fitted, refurbished or warm shell does not establish a complete scope of inclusions or suitability for your intended use. Ask what is physically present, what has been documented, what is promised by the landlord and what still needs professional investigation.

## Use evidence statuses, not a reassuring total score

For every important item, choose one status: **documented**, **advice required**, **work to be scoped**, or **unresolved**. Add the evidence reference, responsible person and decision date. A long list of green ticks should not outweigh one unresolved item that determines whether the premises can support the intended activity.

The checklist is a briefing record, not a building inspection, compliance certificate or financial feasibility assessment. Use the right appointed advisers to evaluate the actual premises and proposed changes.

## Check these seven readiness areas

| Area | Questions for the relevant parties | Useful evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intended use and records | Does the documented use match the proposed business, and what approval questions remain? | Available consent, occupation and plan records plus project-specific advice |
| Layout and access | Does a measured test fit support people, visitors, equipment and movement? | Measured plan, room requirements and designer/access advice where needed |
| Mechanical services | What is known about the existing system and the implications of the proposed layout and use? | Available service records and an appropriate specialist assessment |
| Power, data and connectivity | What capacity, distribution, equipment and service availability must be checked? | Existing information and advice from the relevant providers |
| Fire, amenities and building interfaces | What changes may affect the relevant systems, facilities or common areas? | Current building information and advice from appointed specialists |
| Building condition and unknowns | Which existing conditions or materials need investigation before work is priced? | Relevant records and appropriately qualified investigation |
| Furniture, delivery and occupation | Can the retained and new items suit the plan and reach the site when it is ready? | Product schedule, measured access route and agreed delivery assumptions |

These are questions to allocate, not a technical inspection procedure for the business owner. Do not open building systems, disturb materials or infer capacity from appearance.

## Separate landlord promises from tenant costs

Ask for a written schedule of landlord works, with a responsible party, specification, expected timing and evidence of completion. Keep items that are merely discussed separate from items agreed in the relevant documents. Ask your solicitor about the lease and landlord commitments.

Build a second schedule for tenant works and a third for shared or unresolved interfaces. This reduces the chance of assuming an essential item is included in somebody else's proposal. Connect these schedules to the handover date and the conditions under which the contractor can gain access.

Where intended use or alterations are uncertain, [City of Newcastle's change-of-use guidance](https://newcastle.nsw.gov.au/development/building-and-construction/building-and-development-information-guides/change-of-use) is a starting reference for premises in its council area. Get advice for the actual proposal; a previous tenant's use does not answer every question about yours.

[BUTTON: Discuss the gaps in my premises brief]

## Compare options on the work still needed

When comparing two Newcastle premises, use the same workplace brief for each. Record what can be retained, what needs alteration, what needs investigation and which costs remain unquoted. Distinguish one-off project costs from recurring occupation costs so the business can review the full commitment with its advisers.

**Illustrative example, not a client case:** one office already has meeting rooms but their position may not suit the team or existing services. Another is more open and needs new rooms. A furniture plan and headline rent alone cannot establish the better fitout option. Test the layouts and services implications, then price the agreed scopes.

Avoid turning unverified assumptions into savings. Ask for alternatives that show the change in scope, quality, functionality and timing. Use the [Newcastle fitout cost guide](/blog/commercial-fitout-cost-newcastle-2026) and [construction quote comparison guide](/blog/compare-office-construction-quotes-newcastle) to organise the budget conversation.

## Investigate before locking in the programme

Identify the information that can change the decision: use and approval advice, measured layout, building services, access, landlord works, existing condition and specialist requirements. Ask each adviser what is needed to resolve the question and when they can provide it.

If hazardous materials are a concern, obtain appropriate professional advice. [SafeWork NSW's asbestos guidance](https://www.safework.nsw.gov.au/hazards-a-z/asbestos) directs people to qualified assistance for suspected material. A visual impression or a generic readiness checklist is not an assessment.

Do not assume the same occupation date fits every premises option. Connect investigations, design approvals, ordering, landlord works and construction prerequisites to the programme. If people will work in the office during alterations, use the [occupied-refurbishment guide](/blog/office-refurbishment-newcastle-stay-open) to frame the business-continuity discussion.

## A premises-readiness checklist before committing

- Define the workplace brief and intended use.
- Confirm the address, responsible council and available records.
- Obtain a measured layout and test the proposed workplace requirements.
- Audit retained furniture and equipment.
- Allocate mechanical, power, data and other services questions to the relevant providers.
- Identify fire, amenities, accessibility and common-area interfaces for appropriate advice.
- Obtain relevant existing-condition and hazardous-material information.
- Request a written landlord-works schedule.
- Separate tenant works, shared interfaces and unresolved items.
- Record estimated, quoted and unpriced budget lines separately.
- Test delivery access, site readiness and programme dependencies.
- Take the unresolved questions to the relevant advisers before commitment.

## What can YOS help organise?

Under an agreed client-side engagement, YOS can help connect the business brief with the information being collected, coordinate the appointed advisers' inputs and track scope, budget assumptions and decisions. This helps the business see what is known and what remains unresolved before the next commitment.

YOS does not certify services capacity, planning compliance, building condition or readiness to occupy. Those questions remain with the appropriately appointed parties. The business retains its approval decisions and should obtain the required professional advice for the actual premises.

For the next stage, use the [Newcastle fitout approvals guide](/blog/office-fitout-approvals-newcastle) and the [fitout planning checklist](/blog/office-fitout-newcastle-planning-checklist). The [office size calculator](/resources/office-size-calculator) is an early planning aid, not a substitute for a measured, project-specific design.

## Turn unknowns into the next useful decision

Send the Newcastle suburb, project stage, intended use and the questions you have about the premises. Mention the plans and records you already have. YOS can discuss whether a client-side coordination scope suits the brief and which information to seek next.

## Common questions

### What does fitout-ready office space mean?

For planning purposes, it means understanding how the existing premises compare with the intended workplace and documenting the gaps. A marketing label does not establish suitability, services capacity, compliance or readiness to occupy.

### Can I assess fitout readiness myself?

You can organise the brief, records and open questions, but technical inspections and advice should come from the appropriately qualified providers. Do not inspect building systems or disturb materials yourself based on this checklist.

### Does a warm-shell office include everything needed for our fitout?

The term does not define a complete project scope. Obtain a written schedule of what is present, what the landlord will provide and which tenant works or investigations remain.

### Does YOS certify that the premises are ready?

No. YOS provides client-side coordination under an agreed engagement. Relevant designers, services specialists, planning and certification advisers assess their respective areas; the business retains its commitment decisions.

*General project-planning information only. Confirm the actual requirements with the responsible council and appropriately appointed planning, design, construction, safety, certification and legal advisers. Project scope, timing and availability are confirmed individually.*
